verdict.rationale: Snowflake documents a credit-based consumption pricing model (warehouses consume credits, user-managed control, resizing, resource monitors, cost-anomaly alerts) and lists pricing-tier names on its pricing page, giving a platform engineer some levers to reason about cost. However, hands-on community reports concretely contradict clean bill estimation: one user found costs 'balloon pretty fast' with credits doubling per warehouse size, another explicitly says Snowflake 'lacks query-level attribution of costs and no in-built features for monitoring or recommendations,' and a comparison notes companies can reach $100k/year bills without massive data — all indicating the documented model doesn't translate into reliable upfront estimation. missing for 10: an explicit per-credit/per-tier price table or cost calculator in the evidence, and any documentation walking through a concrete monthly-bill estimation example.
